subject: Social Media
title: Lateral Reading
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lateral Reading.

hook.text: A student checks a website's 'About' page to verify it. A fact-checker opens five new tabs instead. Who's right?

buildup.text: Stanford researchers found students read vertically—staying on one site. Fact-checkers read laterally—leaving fast.

discovery.text: Lateral reading means searching what others say about a source rather than trusting the source's self-description.

twist.text: PhD students were worse than fact-checkers at evaluating sources. Education didn't help. The right technique did.

climax.text: Teaching lateral reading in schools improved students' ability to spot unreliable sources within one semester.

punchline.text: Don't ask the site who it is. Ask the internet.

quiz.question: What is lateral reading?
options: Checking what others say about a source outside that source
